model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the relationship between the co-occurrence number (x-axis, logarithmic scale ranging from 1 to 10⁴) and classification accuracy (ACC, y-axis, linear scale from 40% to 65%) for six different methods: Base (black solid line with circle markers), FT (blue solid line with downward triangle markers), IKE (red solid line with upward triangle markers), MEND (brown solid line with diamond markers), MEMIT (purple solid line with pentagon markers), and ROME (green solid line with square markers). As the co-occurrence number increases, all methods show an upward trend in accuracy, though at different rates. The ROME method consistently achieves the highest accuracy, starting at approximately 51% at a co-occurrence number of 1 and rising to about 66% at 10⁴. MEND and MEMIT follow similar trajectories, reaching approximately 56% and 55% respectively at 10⁴. IKE and FT show moderate gains, ending near 49% and 48%, while the Base method remains relatively flat, increasing only slightly from ~39% to ~44%.
